$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Network security groups. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.nsgs.nsg.crud.title: Network security groups (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.nsgs.security_rules.title: Inbound and outbound security rules (Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/securityRules)
limitations: The 3 default rules per direction (AllowVNetInBound, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound, DenyAllInBound, AllowVNetOutBound, AllowInternetOutBound, DenyAllOutBound) are fixed display rows, not stored ARM resources — they can't be edited or deleted, matching the real portal.

Behaviour comes from the shared netsim evaluator: subnet NSG then NIC NSG inbound (reverse outbound), priorities, the default rules, service tags VirtualNetwork / Internet / AzureLoadBalancer and ASGs — it answers Network Watcher IP flow verify. Azure VMs run on LXD/Multipass offline, not the Docker backend, so NSGs are evaluated, never packet-enforced offline today.

azure.nsgs.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this network security group
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this network security group); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.nsgs.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.nsgs.export_template.title: Export template
limitations: Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the live resource; Bicep and Terraform export are not modelled.

azure.nsgs.iam.title: Access control (IAM)
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), and Check access / My access run the real wildcard + scope-inheritance + notActions + explicit-deny decision — all ENFORCED scoped to this network security group (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view); Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). Deny assignments and Classic administrators remain an honest gap — Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and the legacy Azure Service Management administrator list are not modelled.

azure.nsgs.tools.title: Diagnose and solve problems (remaining tiles), Tasks, Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: Tasks and Support + Troubleshooting are not built, and Diagnose and solve problems' other diagnostic tiles (VM connectivity issue, Network configuration diagnostics, …) remain an honest gap — Tasks is a cross-resource Azure Resource Graph/tagging feature and Support + Troubleshooting opens a Microsoft support request, neither specific to network security groups. Its IP flow verify and Next hop tiles ARE built (azure.nsgs.network_watcher), and Effective security rules is now built (azure.nsgs.effective_rules).

azure.nsgs.effective_rules.title: Effective security rules
limitations: Lists the merged custom + default inbound/outbound rule sets from both the picked network interface's own network security group and its subnet's network security group, in priority order — the same two-NSG picture `az network nic show-effective-nsg` and the real portal's page show. It lists the rule set; it does not simulate a packet (that's IP flow verify, azure.nsgs.network_watcher). Scoped to network interfaces associated with this network security group directly or through their subnet.

azure.nsgs.network_watcher.title: Diagnose and solve problems: IP flow verify, Next hop (Network Watcher)
limitations: IP flow verify and Next hop answer from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim) — the same engine behind AWS Reachability Analyzer and GCP Connectivity Tests — scoped to a virtual machine's network interface in this subscription. Vyomi auto-provisions the regional NetworkWatcher_<location> resource the first time either tool runs in a location, same as the real portal's 'Enable Network Watcher' behaviour. There is no standalone Network Watcher service console (browsing/deleting networkWatchers resources) yet, only these two diagnostic tools reached from the NSG and Virtual network blades.

azure.nsgs.monitoring.title: Alerts, Diagnostic settings, Logs, NSG flow logs
limitations: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings) is a real ARM extension resource scoped to this network security group: logs/metrics are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires, but never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline. Alerts, Logs and NSG flow logs for network security groups remain an honest gap.

azure.nsgs.associations.title: Network interfaces, Subnets (NSG associations)
limitations: The Network interfaces and Subnets lists are real ARM reads (every Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces and virtualNetworks/subnets resource in the subscription whose properties.networkSecurityGroup.id matches this network security group), so an association made via ARM/the CLI/another tool shows up here. The 'Associate' button now really works: it picks from every network interface/subnet in the subscription that has no network security group of its own yet (the same constraint the real portal's Associate dialog enforces) and sets its networkSecurityGroup over ARM.
